astrazeneca.description: AstraZeneca researches, develops and sells prescription medicines to healthcare systems around the world. Its portfolio spans cancer treatments, cardiovascular and kidney disease, respiratory and immune conditions, and rare diseases, with products including Tagrisso, Farxiga and medicines from its Alexion business. Sales of approved treatments fund research into new medicines and additional uses for existing products. The company combines laboratory research, clinical trials, regulatory work and large-scale pharmaceutical manufacturing. Its business depends on demonstrating clinical benefits, securing reimbursement and maintaining reliable supply, while patent expiry and competing treatments continually change the commercial prospects of individual medicines.

shell.description: Shell operates across the energy supply chain, from producing oil and natural gas to supplying fuels, lubricants and electricity to customers. Its liquefied natural gas activities connect gas-producing regions with international markets, while refineries, chemical plants, trading operations and branded service stations provide further routes to market. Revenue comes from selling energy and related products to households, transport operators and industrial customers. The combination of production, processing and distribution gives Shell several sources of earnings, although each responds differently to commodity prices. Large projects, maintenance requirements and changing energy demand make capital allocation and operating reliability central to its business.

hsbc.description: HSBC provides banking and financial services to individuals, businesses and institutions, with particularly important franchises in Hong Kong and the UK and extensive international connections. Its services include deposits, mortgages, business lending, trade finance, payments, wealth management and access to capital markets. The bank earns interest on lending and other assets, alongside fees for transactions, advice and managing investments. Its cross-border network is especially relevant to customers moving goods or money between markets. Performance depends on deposit funding, borrowing demand, credit quality and interest rates, while the diversity of its operations brings exposure to different currencies, economies and regulatory systems.

unilever.description: Unilever develops and markets everyday consumer products across beauty and wellbeing, personal care, home care and foods. Brands such as Dove, Persil, Hellmann's and Knorr reach consumers through supermarkets, smaller retailers, online channels and food-service distributors. The company combines product formulation, brand marketing, manufacturing and distribution, earning revenue from products that households buy repeatedly. Its international reach includes both established consumer markets and economies where spending patterns are still developing. Brand recognition and retail availability support demand, but success also depends on product innovation, competitive pricing and managing ingredient, packaging and transport costs across a complex global supply chain.

relx.description: RELX supplies information, analytics and decision-support tools to professional customers rather than relying primarily on general consumer publishing. Its businesses include Elsevier in scientific and medical information, LexisNexis in legal information and risk analytics, and RX in exhibitions. Customers use its products to research cases, assess risk, detect fraud, conduct scientific work and meet potential commercial partners. Revenue includes subscriptions, usage-based charges and exhibition fees. Its value lies in combining specialised content and datasets with software embedded in professional workflows. Maintaining trusted information, improving search and analysis, and adapting products to artificial intelligence are important parts of its operating model.

british-american-tobacco.description: British American Tobacco manufactures and markets tobacco and nicotine products through an international distribution network. Its portfolio includes cigarette brands such as Dunhill, Lucky Strike and Pall Mall, alongside Vuse vapour products, glo heated products and Velo nicotine pouches. Revenue comes from repeat purchases of consumable products, with pricing, brand choice and retail availability influencing demand. The group is developing newer nicotine categories while managing its established cigarette operations. Its economics are shaped by excise duties, product regulation, marketing restrictions and changes in consumer behaviour. Manufacturing consistency and distribution scale matter, as does the ability to compete across markets with very different legal frameworks.

bp.description: BP produces and trades oil and natural gas and supplies fuels and other energy products to businesses and consumers. Its operations connect upstream production with refining, wholesale trading, service stations, convenience retail and products such as Castrol lubricants. It also participates in electricity, charging and other energy activities. Earnings arise at several stages of the supply chain, including selling resources, processing crude oil and serving end customers. These activities have different sensitivities to energy prices and demand. The business requires substantial spending on infrastructure, maintenance and new projects, making operating efficiency, project selection and the balance between investment and cash generation important features.

gsk.description: GSK develops vaccines and prescription medicines used to prevent and treat disease in markets around the world. Its activities cover specialty medicines, vaccines and established treatments, including work in respiratory disease, immunology, oncology and HIV. Customers ultimately include healthcare systems and patients, with medicines reaching them through regulated distribution and reimbursement arrangements. Revenue from approved products supports research, clinical trials and manufacturing investment. The company must demonstrate safety and clinical effectiveness before launching treatments and continue monitoring them afterwards. Its business is shaped by the strength of its development pipeline, access to healthcare budgets, manufacturing reliability and the loss of exclusivity as products mature.

rolls-royce.description: Rolls-Royce designs and supports engines and power systems for civil aviation, defence and industrial applications. Its civil aerospace business supplies engines for large passenger aircraft and business jets, then maintains them over operating lives that can extend for decades. Defence activities include military aircraft propulsion and naval power systems, while mtu-branded products serve applications such as backup power and marine propulsion. Revenue combines equipment sales with servicing, spare parts and long-term support agreements. Aircraft utilisation therefore matters alongside new engine deliveries. Engineering capability, product reliability and maintenance efficiency are central to the business, which requires sustained investment in technology and manufacturing.

lseg.description: London Stock Exchange Group provides financial data, analytics and market infrastructure to banks, investment managers, companies and other institutions. Its activities extend well beyond the stock exchange itself, encompassing trading and clearing services, FTSE Russell indices, market information and risk-intelligence tools. Customers use these products to price assets, build portfolios, execute transactions and perform compliance checks. Revenue comes from subscriptions, licences and fees linked to financial-market activity. Its products often sit within customers' daily workflows, making dependable data and system availability particularly important. The business combines recurring information services with transaction-sensitive operations and requires ongoing investment in technology, connectivity and data quality.

diageo.description: Diageo produces and markets alcoholic drinks, with a portfolio spanning whisky, tequila, vodka, rum, liqueurs and beer. Its brands include Johnnie Walker, Guinness, Smirnoff, Baileys and Don Julio, distributed through retailers, bars, restaurants and travel-related channels. Revenue depends on sales volumes, pricing and the mix of products consumers choose. Brand heritage and marketing help differentiate drinks, while distribution relationships determine availability across markets. Some products, particularly aged spirits, require inventory to be produced and stored years before sale. The business is influenced by household spending, drinking preferences, distributor stock levels and alcohol regulation, alongside agricultural inputs, packaging and currency movements.

rio-tinto.description: Rio Tinto extracts and processes minerals used in construction, manufacturing, transport and energy infrastructure. Its portfolio includes iron ore, aluminium, copper and lithium, supported by mines, processing plants, transport facilities and other industrial assets. Customers buy materials whose prices are largely determined in international commodity markets. Revenue therefore reflects both production volumes and market prices, while profitability depends on resource quality, extraction costs and efficient logistics. Developing or expanding a mine requires major investment and long planning periods. The group also manages environmental obligations and relationships with host communities, with access to energy, water and infrastructure affecting the economics of individual operations.

national-grid.description: National Grid owns and operates energy networks that move electricity and gas between producers and customers. Its activities include electricity transmission and distribution in the UK and regulated utility operations in the northeastern United States. These networks earn revenue under regulatory arrangements that govern charges, service standards and investment returns. The company also participates in infrastructure such as electricity interconnectors. Its business is built around maintaining and expanding long-lived physical assets rather than simply selling energy at market prices. Connecting new generation and meeting changing electricity demand require substantial capital spending, while financing costs, regulatory decisions and reliable network operation are important to performance.

barclays.description: Barclays combines UK retail and corporate banking with international investment banking, private banking and a US consumer-banking business. Individuals use its current accounts, mortgages, savings and credit cards, while companies access lending, payments, financing advice and capital markets. Revenue comes from interest earned on assets and fees associated with banking and investment services. This mix gives the group exposure to both everyday customer activity and financial-market conditions. Its performance depends on funding costs, lending margins, credit losses and demand for transactions or advice. Managing capital, liquidity and operational risk is central to serving customers across different banking businesses and jurisdictions.

compass.description: Compass Group provides outsourced catering and related support services to organisations such as employers, hospitals, schools, universities and sporting venues. Rather than depending on a single restaurant brand, it operates food services at client sites under contracts adapted to different settings. Revenue comes from meals served and agreed service arrangements, with economics varying according to contract terms and customer attendance. Purchasing scale, menu planning, staffing and kitchen operations are central to delivery. Its broad client base gives exposure to multiple end markets, while retaining contracts and winning new outsourcing work support growth. Food inflation, labour availability and service quality directly affect day-to-day performance.

bae-systems.description: BAE Systems develops and supports defence, aerospace and security equipment for government customers and their partners. Its activities include combat aircraft, naval ships and submarines, armoured vehicles, electronic systems, munitions and cyber capabilities. Revenue is largely generated through programmes that can run for many years, combining development, production and ongoing support. This creates substantial engineering and manufacturing requirements and close relationships with national defence authorities. Orders depend on government priorities and procurement budgets, while delivery depends on specialist staff and complex supply chains. Contract structures, project execution and the cost of meeting technical requirements are important to the profitability of individual programmes.

lloyds.description: Lloyds Banking Group provides financial services primarily to customers in the UK through brands including Lloyds Bank, Halifax, Bank of Scotland and Scottish Widows. Its activities span current accounts, savings, mortgages, consumer credit, business banking, insurance, pensions and investments. The group earns interest from lending and fees from financial services, supported by a large deposit base. Its domestic focus connects performance closely with UK household finances, housing activity and business conditions. Mortgage pricing, deposit competition and credit losses influence earnings, while digital banking and branch services support customer relationships. Insurance and retirement products add longer-term financial relationships alongside its core banking operations.

3i.description: 3i is an investment company that owns stakes in private businesses and participates in infrastructure investing. Its private-equity approach involves backing established companies and working with management teams to improve operations and support expansion. The discount retailer Action is a particularly significant holding, making its trading and valuation important to the group's overall results. Returns come from changes in investment values, distributions and realisations, with investment-management activities providing another income source. Unlike a conventional manufacturer or retailer, 3i's reported performance reflects the businesses it owns and how those interests are valued. Capital allocation, portfolio concentration and the timing of exits are therefore central considerations.

experian.description: Experian supplies credit information, data analytics and software to businesses and consumers. Lenders use its information to assess applications and manage existing customers, while other clients use its tools for identity checks, fraud prevention, marketing and operational decisions. Its consumer services help individuals understand credit information and access related products. Revenue comes from data services, software, subscriptions and customer activity across these offerings. The company operates internationally, with different markets having distinct credit systems and data rules. Its business depends on maintaining accurate information, safeguarding personal data and embedding useful tools into customer workflows, alongside the level of borrowing and commercial activity.

glencore.description: Glencore combines the production of commodities with a large marketing and trading operation. Its industrial assets produce resources including copper, cobalt, zinc, nickel and coal, while its marketing business sources and supplies materials from its own operations and third parties. Customers include manufacturers, energy users and processors around the world. Revenue comes from commodity sales, with earnings influenced by production costs, market prices and the margins available from moving materials between locations and customers. The trading model requires logistics expertise, working capital and careful risk management. Mining operations add long-term asset exposure, environmental obligations and substantial maintenance and development requirements.

admiral.description: Admiral Group provides insurance and personal-lending products, with UK motor insurance forming a central part of its business. It also offers products such as home, travel and pet insurance and operates insurance businesses in several European markets. Customers buy cover through its brands and distribution channels, while the group uses underwriting, pricing and claims management to assess and handle risk. Revenue includes insurance-related income and lending returns. Its model incorporates arrangements that share some insurance risk with partners. Performance depends on pricing policies appropriately, controlling claims costs and retaining customers, with repair inflation, weather events and changes in driving patterns affecting results.

airtel-africa.description: Airtel Africa operates mobile telecommunications and mobile-money services across African markets. Customers use its networks for voice calls, messaging and internet access, while Airtel Money supports transfers, merchant payments and other financial transactions. Revenue comes from connectivity usage, customer plans and fees associated with mobile-money activity. The business serves markets where smartphones and digital financial services can broaden access to communications and commerce. Delivering these services requires spectrum, network equipment, distribution outlets and reliable power. Customer growth and data usage matter, but local currencies, affordability, regulation and the cost of expanding network coverage also shape the economics of its operations.

alliance-witan.description: Alliance Witan is a listed investment trust holding a portfolio of global equities. Its investment manager, WTW, allocates capital among specialist managers whose selections are combined into one portfolio, bringing together different investment styles and areas of expertise. Shareholders gain exposure to the underlying companies through shares in the trust rather than owning each holding directly. Returns reflect portfolio gains and losses, dividend income, fees and any borrowing costs. The trust's own share price can differ from the value of its investments. Its distinguishing feature is the multi-manager structure, which aims to diversify stock selection while maintaining a coordinated approach to the overall portfolio.

anglo-american.description: Anglo American is a mining group supplying materials used in industry and infrastructure, with copper and premium iron ore central to its portfolio and crop nutrients part of its development activities. Its work spans resource exploration, mine development, extraction, processing and logistics. Revenue is generated by selling commodities to industrial customers, so both production volumes and internationally determined prices affect results. Mining assets require substantial investment before they produce cash and continued spending throughout their operating lives. Resource quality, energy and water availability, project delivery and relationships with host governments are important to the business, particularly while the group reshapes its asset portfolio.

antofagasta.description: Antofagasta is a mining group centred on copper production in Chile, with operations including Los Pelambres and Centinela. Its mines sell copper in forms such as concentrates and cathodes and also recover by-products including gold and molybdenum. A transport business serves industrial customers in northern Chile. Revenue depends on output and commodity prices, while mine profitability reflects ore quality, processing efficiency and the cost of energy, water and labour. Expansion projects require long planning periods and substantial capital. Its concentration in copper provides exposure to demand from electricity networks, construction and manufacturing, with environmental permissions and water infrastructure particularly important to operations.

associated-british-foods.description: Associated British Foods combines the Primark clothing retailer with businesses in grocery products, ingredients, sugar and agriculture. Primark sells fashion and household products through a value-focused store network, while the food businesses supply consumers and commercial customers with branded groceries, baking ingredients and other products. Revenue is therefore spread across activities with different customers and economic drivers. Clothing demand and store productivity matter to retail, while crop conditions, commodity inputs and industrial demand influence food and agriculture. The group's decentralised structure allows its businesses to operate in specialised markets, supported by shared capital allocation and a portfolio that spans both consumer and business spending.

auto-trader.description: Auto Trader operates a digital automotive marketplace connecting vehicle buyers with retailers and private sellers in the UK. Dealers pay for advertising and related tools that help them present stock, understand pricing and manage their online presence. Consumers use the platform to compare vehicles and research potential purchases, creating the audience that makes it useful to sellers. Additional activities include services related to vehicle leasing and transactions. The business relies on attracting a broad selection of stock and a large pool of prospective buyers. Dealer profitability, vehicle supply and the effectiveness of its software products influence demand for its paid services.

aviva.description: Aviva provides insurance, retirement and wealth products to individuals and businesses, with major operations in the UK, Ireland and Canada. Its offerings include motor and home insurance, commercial cover, life protection, pensions and annuities, alongside investment-management services. Revenue and earnings arise through underwriting, investment-related activities and charges for savings and financial products. General insurance depends on pricing and claims costs, while retirement products involve managing liabilities and assets over much longer periods. Its combination of businesses creates several sources of customer income, but also requires careful capital and risk management. Distribution partnerships, customer retention and service quality support relationships across different life stages.

barratt-redrow.description: Barratt Redrow builds homes in the UK under brands including Barratt Homes, David Wilson Homes and Redrow. The business buys land, obtains planning permission, develops infrastructure and constructs properties for private buyers and housing partners. Revenue is primarily recognised through home sales, making completions, selling prices and construction costs important to results. Its different brands serve a range of buyers and locations, while national scale supports purchasing and development capacity. The business requires capital to be committed to land and construction before homes are sold. Mortgage affordability, planning constraints, build quality and the pace of customer reservations therefore influence both profitability and cash flow.

beazley.description: Beazley is a specialist insurer providing cover for complex commercial risks, including cyber incidents, professional liabilities, property losses and marine-related exposures. It works through insurance-market relationships and distribution channels to serve businesses across international markets. Revenue comes from underwriting insurance, with investment income also contributing while funds are held to meet claims. Its value to customers lies in specialist risk assessment and handling events that can be difficult to insure through standard products. Profitability depends on charging appropriate premiums, controlling exposure and estimating future claims. Cyber events, catastrophes and legal developments can affect multiple policyholders, making portfolio management and reinsurance important to the model.

british-land.description: British Land owns, develops and manages commercial property in the UK, with a focus on London campuses and retail parks. It supplies space to office occupiers, retailers and other businesses, earning rental income under leases and seeking to improve asset values through development and active management. Its work includes attracting tenants, upgrading buildings and managing the surrounding environment. Portfolio performance depends on occupancy, rents, operating costs and the values buyers assign to property income. Development adds opportunities but also construction and letting requirements. Financing costs and changes in how businesses use physical space influence returns across assets with long operating lives.

bt.description: BT Group provides fixed and mobile communications through businesses serving consumers, companies and wholesale customers. Its activities include broadband, mobile connectivity under EE, enterprise networking and Openreach infrastructure used by multiple service providers. Revenue comes from subscriptions, access charges and communications services, with customer relationships often extending over recurring contracts. Building and maintaining fibre and mobile networks requires substantial capital investment and technical operations. Its economics depend on network utilisation, customer retention and the cost of delivering reliable service. Competition affects retail pricing, while regulation is particularly important to wholesale infrastructure, where network availability and access terms influence the wider UK communications market.

bunzl.description: Bunzl distributes everyday operating supplies that businesses need but generally do not manufacture themselves. Products include food packaging, cleaning materials, safety equipment and healthcare consumables for customers such as retailers, caterers, hospitals and industrial companies. It earns revenue by sourcing products from suppliers and delivering them through specialised distribution businesses. Customers can simplify purchasing by obtaining multiple essential items through one relationship, with service reliability and availability supporting repeat orders. Its model depends on procurement, inventory management and efficient logistics. Growth comes from existing customer activity and acquisitions, while input-price changes, product mix and the cost of serving customers affect distribution margins.

centrica.description: Centrica supplies energy and related services to households and businesses, with British Gas a central UK brand and Bord Gais Energy serving Ireland. Its activities include electricity and gas supply, boiler installation and maintenance, energy trading and other energy assets and solutions. Revenue comes from customer bills, service agreements and wholesale activities. Retail supply requires balancing energy purchases with customer consumption, while service operations depend on skilled engineers and reliable scheduling. The different businesses respond differently to wholesale prices and weather. Regulation, customer service, credit management and the ability to manage volatile energy markets are important to the group's operational and financial performance.

coca-cola-hbc.description: Coca-Cola HBC produces, packages and distributes beverages across a range of European and emerging markets, including Nigeria. As a bottling partner, it handles local manufacturing, logistics and customer relationships for Coca-Cola products alongside other drinks in its portfolio. Customers include supermarkets, convenience stores, restaurants and hospitality operators. Revenue comes from beverage sales, with volumes, pricing and the mix of pack sizes and products influencing results. Its role is operationally different from owning the Coca-Cola brand itself. Production efficiency, distribution reach and retail execution matter, while weather, consumer spending, packaging costs and local market conditions can change demand and margins.

convatec.description: Convatec develops medical products used in managing chronic conditions, including wound care, ostomy care, continence care and infusion-related applications. Its products support patients in hospitals, community settings and at home, often requiring repeat purchases of consumable items. Revenue comes from supplying these products through healthcare providers, distributors and patient-service channels. Clinical performance, comfort and ease of use are important because products may form part of daily care. The business combines medical-device development with manufacturing and customer support. Demand depends on treatment needs and healthcare access, while reimbursement arrangements, quality standards and reliable supply influence how products reach patients and generate recurring revenue.

croda-international.description: Croda develops specialty ingredients used in consumer-care products, life sciences and industrial applications. Its customers incorporate these materials into products such as cosmetics, personal care formulations, medicines and crop treatments. Revenue comes from ingredients whose value often depends on a specific function, including texture, stability, delivery or performance, rather than simply the volume of raw material supplied. Working with customers on formulations can create long-standing commercial relationships. The business combines chemistry research, technical support and specialised manufacturing. Customer product launches, inventory cycles and demand in end markets influence sales, while manufacturing efficiency and the success of differentiated ingredients affect profitability.

dcc.description: DCC supplies energy products and services through distribution businesses serving domestic, commercial and industrial customers. Its energy activities include liquid gas, transport and heating fuels, electricity-related solutions and services that help customers manage energy use. Distribution networks, local customer relationships and dependable delivery are important to its model. Revenue comes from product sales and associated services, with results influenced by volumes, product margins and operating efficiency. The group has been reshaping its portfolio around energy, so business disposals and investment decisions also matter. Weather, customer activity and the pace of changes in heating and transport technology affect demand across its markets.

diploma.description: Diploma supplies specialised technical products through businesses operating in controls, seals and life sciences. Its offerings range from wiring and connection components to sealing products, fluid-power equipment and healthcare instruments and consumables. Customers often need these products for maintenance, production or clinical work, where availability and technical support can matter more than a small difference in purchase price. Revenue comes from product sales and related services across industrial and healthcare markets. Its operating companies focus on particular niches, supported by group-level investment and acquisitions. Performance depends on customer activity, product expertise and inventory availability, alongside the ability to integrate and develop acquired businesses.

endeavour-mining.description: Endeavour Mining produces gold from operations in West Africa, including mines in Senegal, Cote d'Ivoire and Burkina Faso. Its activities cover exploration, mine development, extraction and processing, with sales linked to the international gold market. Production volumes, ore grades and recovery rates determine how much gold can be sold, while energy, labour and maintenance affect costs. New projects and exploration help replace reserves as existing deposits are mined. Its regional focus creates operating expertise but also exposure to local security, government and infrastructure conditions. Reliable execution and disciplined investment are important because mine construction requires substantial spending before production generates revenue.

entain.description: Entain operates sports-betting and gaming businesses through online services and retail venues. Brands such as Ladbrokes, Coral and bwin connect customers with sports wagering, casino games and other betting products in regulated markets. Revenue is based on gaming activity after customer winnings, with the precise economics varying across products and jurisdictions. Technology, brand marketing and customer experience support its digital operations, while physical shops provide another distribution channel. The business depends on maintaining licences and meeting rules on customer protection and responsible gambling. Sporting calendars, competitive promotions, taxes and the cost of acquiring and retaining customers all influence commercial performance.

fandc-investment-trust.description: F&C Investment Trust holds a diversified portfolio of global investments, giving shareholders access to many companies through a single listed vehicle. Its portfolio includes public equities and exposure to private equity, spreading investments across markets and business sectors. Returns come from dividends and changes in the value of underlying holdings, after management costs and other expenses. The trust structure allows its shares to trade independently of the portfolio's net asset value, creating a premium or discount. Its broad approach differs from a company selling products or services: performance primarily reflects investment selection, market movements, currency exposure and the way portfolio capital is allocated over time.

fresnillo.description: Fresnillo mines silver and gold in Mexico, with operations also producing metals such as lead and zinc as by-products. Its business spans exploration, mine development, extraction and processing, supported by long-lived mining assets. Revenue depends on the quantity of metal produced and prices in international markets. Ore grades, processing recoveries and operating costs influence the profitability of individual mines, while new development is needed to sustain production as reserves are depleted. The company's geographic focus makes local infrastructure, water, energy and permitting important. Precious-metal demand affects selling prices, but operational execution determines how efficiently those market conditions translate into cash generation.

games-workshop.description: Games Workshop creates and sells miniature tabletop games and the fictional worlds that support them, most notably Warhammer. Its core business includes models, paints, rulebooks and related hobby products sold through its own stores, independent retailers and online channels. It also earns licensing income when partners use its intellectual property in products such as video games. The model combines design and manufacturing with an enthusiast community that collects, builds, paints and plays with its products. New releases and engagement with established settings help support repeat purchases. Brand ownership and creative development are central, alongside manufacturing capacity, distribution and the appeal of its hobby ecosystem.

haleon.description: Haleon develops and markets consumer-healthcare products that people can often buy without a prescription. Its portfolio includes oral-care, pain-relief, digestive-health and vitamin products, with brands such as Sensodyne, Panadol, Advil and Centrum. Products reach consumers through pharmacies, supermarkets, other retailers and online channels. Revenue depends on repeat purchases, brand recognition and the perceived effectiveness of its products. The business combines scientific formulation, marketing and manufacturing, with professional recommendations relevant in areas such as oral health. Consumer spending and seasonal illness can affect demand, while product regulation, quality control and ingredient or packaging costs influence operations across its international markets.

halma.description: Halma owns a group of specialised technology businesses serving safety, environmental and healthcare markets. Its products help detect hazards, monitor water and other environmental conditions, support medical care and protect people or infrastructure. Customers typically buy solutions to specific technical problems, where reliability and compliance are important. Revenue comes from these niche operating companies, which have considerable independence within the group. Halma allocates capital to product development and acquisitions that extend its portfolio. The business model combines specialist expertise with exposure to needs such as safer workplaces and better diagnostics, while performance depends on maintaining product quality and developing businesses in their individual markets.

hiscox.description: Hiscox provides specialist insurance and reinsurance to individuals, businesses and other insurers. Its activities include small-business cover, insurance for valuable personal assets and larger commercial risks handled through the London market. Reinsurance allows it to take on portions of risks originally written by other insurers. Income comes from underwriting and investing funds held against future claims. Its model depends on understanding complex risks, setting appropriate premiums and controlling aggregate exposure. Claims from catastrophes or liability events can emerge unevenly over time. Distribution through brokers, partners and direct channels gives it several routes to customers, while underwriting discipline is central to profitability.

howden-joinery.description: Howden Joinery supplies kitchens, joinery products and related equipment primarily to trade customers through its Howdens depot network. Builders and installers buy products for their own projects, making local availability, service and relationships with tradespeople important to the model. The company combines product sourcing and manufacturing with distribution through depots that hold stock close to customers. Revenue comes from kitchens and associated items rather than charging homeowners directly for a full installation service. Demand is linked to renovation and construction activity. Product design, depot productivity and supply-chain efficiency influence performance, alongside the ability to offer tradespeople reliable access to complete kitchen solutions.

imi.description: IMI develops engineering products that control the movement of fluids and gases in industrial systems. Its technologies are used in applications such as process operations, manufacturing automation and building climate control, where precision and reliability can be essential. Customers buy components, systems and related support that help equipment operate safely and efficiently. Revenue comes from original equipment requirements and replacement or service demand across different industrial markets. The business combines engineering design with specialised manufacturing and technical customer relationships. Demand depends on investment and maintenance activity in its end markets, while product performance, energy efficiency and the ability to solve difficult control problems support its competitive position.

imperial-brands.description: Imperial Brands manufactures and distributes tobacco and nicotine products across international markets. Its portfolio includes established cigarette and tobacco brands alongside newer product formats such as vapour, heated tobacco and oral nicotine. Revenue comes from repeat consumer purchases through retail and distribution channels. The business manages a mature tobacco market in which pricing, brand choice and cost control are important, while investing selectively in alternative categories. Excise taxes and restrictions on packaging, advertising and product availability strongly influence how it operates. Performance depends on managing sales volumes and product mix, maintaining distribution and adapting to changing consumer preferences within different national regulatory frameworks.

informa.description: Informa organises business-to-business events and provides specialist knowledge through academic publishing and related services. Its exhibitions and conferences connect suppliers with potential customers, while its publishing activities distribute research and professional content, including through Taylor & Francis. Revenue comes from exhibitors, sponsorship, attendance and information products such as subscriptions or publishing services. Events depend on delivering useful commercial connections, whereas knowledge products rely on trusted content and distribution. The combination serves specialised professional communities across many industries. Customer marketing budgets, event scheduling and publishing models influence performance, while maintaining strong brands and recurring relationships helps support repeat business across its portfolio.

intercontinental-hotels.description: InterContinental Hotels Group, or IHG, operates a portfolio of hotel brands including Holiday Inn, InterContinental and Crowne Plaza. Much of its business involves franchising brands or managing hotels owned by third parties, rather than owning every hotel building itself. It earns fees linked to hotel activity and management arrangements, supported by reservation systems, loyalty programmes and brand standards. Hotel owners gain distribution and operating support, while guests receive recognisable brands across destinations. Performance depends on travel demand, room rates and the number of hotels using its systems. Maintaining service consistency and attracting owners to develop or convert hotels are important to expansion.

intermediate-capital.description: Intermediate Capital Group, also known as ICG, manages alternative investments for institutional clients and other investors. Its activities include private credit, private equity-related strategies and investments in real assets, providing capital to businesses outside conventional public markets. The group earns management fees and, where applicable, performance-related income, while also investing its own capital alongside strategies. Relationships with investors support fundraising, and relationships with borrowers or portfolio companies create investment opportunities. Its business depends on deploying funds effectively, managing credit and investment risk and delivering outcomes that encourage future commitments. Market conditions influence fundraising, valuations and the timing of investment realisations.

intertek.description: Intertek provides testing, inspection, certification and assurance services to organisations that need to verify products, processes or assets. Customers use its laboratories and technical expertise to assess safety, quality, performance and compliance with standards. Its work spans consumer goods, industrial equipment, supply chains, energy and other markets. Revenue comes from testing assignments, inspections and ongoing service arrangements, with demand often linked to production, trade and regulation. Independent verification can help customers access markets and reduce the risk of product failures. The business depends on technical credibility, laboratory capacity and service responsiveness, while local expertise supports customers operating across different regulatory environments.

international-consolidated-airlines.description: International Airlines Group brings together airlines including British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus and Vueling. Its businesses carry passengers and cargo across short-haul and long-haul networks, supported by loyalty and other travel-related activities. Revenue comes from tickets, ancillary services and freight, with fares and capacity managed across routes and seasons. Different airline brands serve different customer segments and geographic strengths. The business requires significant spending on aircraft, maintenance, staff and airport access, while fuel is a major operating input. Performance depends on travel demand, seat utilisation and pricing, alongside reliable operations and the ability to manage disruption across complex flight networks.

jd-sports-fashion.description: JD Sports Fashion sells sports-inspired footwear, apparel and accessories through stores and digital channels in international markets. It works with major sportswear brands and uses its retail formats to reach consumers interested in trainers, fashion and athletic styles. Revenue comes mainly from merchandise sales, with profitability influenced by product mix, stock availability and the level of discounting required. Brand relationships and access to desirable products help shape its offering. The business combines merchandising with store operations and online fulfilment. Consumer confidence, fashion preferences and promotional competition affect demand, while expansion requires careful management of inventory, retail costs and newly acquired or opened businesses.

kingfisher.description: Kingfisher is a home-improvement retailer operating brands including B&Q, Screwfix, Castorama and Brico Depot. It sells tools, building materials, kitchens, bathrooms and other products to households and trade professionals through stores and online channels. Revenue depends on renovation, repair and maintenance spending, with customer needs ranging from small purchases to major projects. Its different retail formats combine broad ranges with convenient access for tradespeople. Sourcing scale, own-brand products and distribution support the commercial model. Housing activity, consumer budgets and seasonal demand influence sales, while inventory management and the efficiency of stores and fulfilment operations are important to profitability.

land-securities.description: Land Securities, commonly known as Landsec, owns and develops commercial property in the UK. Its portfolio includes workplaces, retail destinations and development opportunities intended to create or improve urban locations. Revenue primarily comes from rent paid by occupiers, while development and asset management can change the value and earning potential of properties. The business must attract tenants, maintain buildings and decide where to invest or recycle capital. Results are influenced by occupancy, rental growth, property valuations and financing costs. Changes in office use and shopping patterns affect demand, making location, building quality and the long-term adaptability of its assets important.

legal-and-general.description: Legal & General provides retirement, insurance and investment services to individuals and institutions. Its activities include managing investment portfolios, offering annuities and taking on pension obligations from corporate pension schemes. Revenue and earnings arise from asset-management fees, insurance operations and returns generated while managing long-term liabilities. Customers rely on it for services that can extend over decades, so asset selection, capital strength and liability management are fundamental. The business is influenced by pension demand, market levels, interest rates and longevity assumptions. Its combination of investment expertise and retirement products connects the management of savings with the provision of future income.

londonmetric-property.description: LondonMetric Property owns commercial real estate let to occupiers under leases intended to provide recurring rental income. Its portfolio includes logistics buildings and properties used for activities such as healthcare, convenience retail and leisure. The business selects assets and tenants, manages leases and reallocates capital through acquisitions and disposals. Revenue depends on rents, occupancy and contractual reviews, while property values reflect both the expected income and market financing conditions. Longer leases can improve visibility but make tenant quality important. Its investment approach focuses on buildings that meet occupiers' operational needs, with borrowing costs and the terms of lease agreements influencing shareholder returns.

mandg.description: M&G provides savings, investment and retirement products to individuals and institutions. Its asset-management operations run portfolios across public and private markets, while its life and savings business serves policyholders through pensions, annuities and other long-term products. Revenue includes investment-management fees and income associated with managing insurance and savings contracts. The businesses connect customer assets with investment capabilities, but have different capital requirements and cash-flow patterns. Performance depends on investment outcomes, customer inflows and withdrawals, market conditions and the cost of administering policies. Managing long-term commitments alongside new business is an important part of maintaining customer relationships and financial resilience.

marks-and-spencer.description: Marks & Spencer sells food, clothing, home and beauty products through stores and digital channels. Its food offering emphasises own-brand products, while its fashion and home businesses serve customers across everyday and seasonal purchases. The group also reaches customers through international arrangements and its interest in Ocado Retail. Revenue comes from retail sales, with different categories having distinct purchase frequencies and margin structures. Product quality, value and availability influence customer loyalty. The business combines merchandising, supplier relationships and store operations with online fulfilment, while consumer spending, stock management and the cost of running and modernising its retail estate affect performance.

melrose-industries.description: Melrose Industries operates in aerospace through businesses that develop and manufacture components and systems for aircraft and engines. Its activities include engine structures and parts, airframe components and electrical systems for civil and defence applications. Customers include major aircraft and engine manufacturers, with programmes often lasting many years. Revenue comes from production work and, in parts of the engine business, aftermarket-related activity. Its model depends on engineering qualifications, manufacturing precision and long-term positions on aircraft programmes. Demand is influenced by aircraft build rates and fleet usage, while supply-chain reliability, production efficiency and investment in new technologies determine how effectively orders become earnings.

natwest.description: NatWest Group provides banking and financial services centred on the UK, serving households, businesses and wealth-management clients. Its offerings include current accounts, savings, mortgages, commercial lending, payments and private banking. Revenue comes from interest on lending and other assets, together with fees for financial services. Customer deposits provide an important funding base, linking everyday banking relationships with lending capacity. The group's performance is closely connected to UK economic conditions, borrower confidence and interest rates. Credit quality, competition for deposits and operating efficiency affect earnings, while digital services and relationship banking help support customer retention across its retail and commercial franchises.

next.description: Next sells clothing, homeware and beauty products through stores and online channels, combining its own ranges with third-party brands. Its operations also include consumer credit and Total Platform services that provide capabilities such as websites, warehousing and distribution to other retailers. Revenue therefore comes from merchandise sales and additional commercial services. Its online infrastructure allows the group to reach customers beyond its physical stores and support partner brands. Product selection, inventory discipline and fulfilment efficiency are central to the model. Consumer spending and fashion demand influence sales, while the balance between stores, digital retail and platform services affects how the business develops.

pearson.description: Pearson provides educational content, assessments and learning services to students, institutions and employers. Its activities include qualifications and testing, higher-education course materials, English-language learning and workforce skills. Revenue comes from products, digital subscriptions, assessment fees and service arrangements with organisations or learners. Customers use its tools to learn material, demonstrate competence and progress into further study or employment. The business depends on trusted content and reliable assessment, with technology changing how both are delivered. Demand varies across education systems and employment markets, while adoption by institutions, learner engagement and the move from printed materials to digital services influence commercial performance.

pershing-square.description: Pershing Square Holdings is a listed investment company providing exposure to a portfolio managed by Pershing Square Capital Management. Its approach involves a relatively concentrated set of investments, making the performance of individual holdings important to overall results. Shareholders participate through the investment company's shares, whose market price can differ from the net value of the underlying portfolio. Returns reflect investment gains and losses, income, expenses and any hedging or financing arrangements. The structure is therefore different from an operating company selling goods or services. Portfolio decisions, concentration, market conditions and the discount or premium at which its shares trade are central to understanding performance.

persimmon.description: Persimmon builds homes in the UK through brands including Persimmon Homes and Charles Church, alongside activity supplying housing partners. It acquires land, secures permissions and constructs residential developments before selling completed homes. The group also manufactures some building components, including timber-frame products, bricks and roof tiles, supporting its construction supply chain. Revenue depends on home completions and selling prices, while profitability reflects land, labour and material costs. Capital is committed ahead of sales, making development timing and customer demand important to cash flow. Mortgage affordability, planning requirements and build quality influence the pace and economics of its projects.

phoenix.description: Standard Life, formerly Phoenix Group, provides long-term savings and retirement products, including workplace pensions, individual savings and annuities. Its activities combine managing existing policy books with attracting new retirement and pension business. Customers use its products to accumulate savings or convert them into future income, while the group manages assets and obligations over extended periods. Earnings depend on policy charges, insurance economics and the management of capital and investments. The business requires careful matching of assets to future commitments and efficient administration of large policy populations. Customer retention, pension demand, interest rates and longevity assumptions influence outcomes across its different products.

prudential.description: Prudential provides life and health insurance and asset-management services with a focus on Asia and Africa. Its products help customers protect income, pay for healthcare and build longer-term savings. Distribution through agents, banks and other channels connects the business with households in markets that have different insurance needs and levels of financial development. Revenue and earnings depend on policies sold, existing customer relationships and the management of long-term commitments. The business combines local distribution with group-level investment and risk capabilities. Economic conditions, healthcare costs, customer retention and regulatory capital requirements influence performance across the countries in which it operates.

reckitt-benckiser.description: Reckitt develops and markets branded health, hygiene and nutrition products used by consumers around the world. Its portfolio includes names such as Dettol, Durex, Gaviscon, Nurofen, Finish and Lysol, alongside infant-nutrition products. Goods reach customers through pharmacies, supermarkets and online retailers. Revenue comes from repeat purchases, supported by brand familiarity, product performance and retail availability. The business combines formulation, marketing and manufacturing across categories with different seasonal and consumer-demand patterns. Product safety and quality are particularly important in health and nutrition. Pricing, competition and ingredient or packaging costs influence margins, while changes to the portfolio affect the mix of businesses represented by the group.

rentokil-initial.description: Rentokil Initial provides pest-control and hygiene services to businesses and households across international markets. Technicians inspect sites, treat infestations and provide ongoing prevention, while hygiene operations supply and maintain products used in washrooms and other facilities. Revenue includes recurring service contracts and one-off treatments. Its model depends on local service networks, where having customers close together can improve technician productivity and reduce travel costs. Customers value reliable prevention and compliance support, particularly in food, hospitality and healthcare settings. Retention, route efficiency and staff capability influence performance, while acquisitions expand coverage and create a need to integrate operations and customer systems.

sage.description: Sage develops software that helps small and medium-sized businesses manage accounting, payroll, people and other operational processes. Products such as Sage Intacct support financial management, while other applications serve different business sizes and requirements. Revenue comes mainly from software subscriptions and related support, creating ongoing relationships with customers who rely on the systems for daily work. Accountants and business partners also help distribute and implement its products. The company combines software development with customer service and compliance updates. Demand depends on the value customers see in automation and accurate records, while retention and the adoption of cloud services support the recurring-revenue model.

j-sainsbury.description: J Sainsbury operates UK food and general-merchandise retail businesses, including Sainsbury's supermarkets and convenience stores, Argos and clothing under Tu. Its Nectar loyalty activities connect customer offers with data and marketing services. Revenue comes largely from selling products through stores and online channels, with groceries generating frequent shopping visits and other categories offering different spending patterns. The business relies on purchasing, distribution and store efficiency to deliver availability and value. Competition is intense, making pricing, product quality and service important. Household budgets, seasonal demand and wage or logistics costs affect results, while the integration of digital orders and physical locations shapes fulfilment operations.

schroders.description: Schroders manages investments for institutions, intermediaries and private clients across public and private markets. Its offerings include equity and bond portfolios, multi-asset strategies, real assets and wealth-management services. Revenue is primarily generated through fees linked to client assets, with some products also earning performance-related income. The business depends on attracting and retaining capital by providing investment expertise, suitable products and service. Market movements change the value of assets under management even without customer inflows or withdrawals. Its broad client base and range of strategies provide different sources of demand, while investment performance, fee competition and distribution relationships influence commercial outcomes.

scottish-mortgage-investment-trust.description: Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust invests in public and private companies selected for their long-term growth potential. Managed by Baillie Gifford, it seeks businesses benefiting from major changes in technology, consumer behaviour and other areas of the economy. Shareholders receive exposure through a listed trust whose share price can trade above or below the value of its portfolio. Returns depend on the underlying companies, valuation changes and expenses rather than sales of a product made by the trust itself. Private holdings require valuation judgements and are less easily traded than listed shares, while the growth-focused approach can produce substantial differences from broad-market performance.

segro.description: SEGRO owns, manages and develops warehouses and industrial property in the UK and continental Europe. Its assets include urban space near major population centres and larger distribution facilities located around transport networks. Customers use these buildings for logistics, storage, production and other operating needs. Revenue comes from rent, while development and asset management can increase future income and property value. Occupancy, lease terms and rental growth are important to results. The business requires investment in buildings and land, with financing costs and property yields affecting valuations. Location and the availability of suitable space influence its ability to attract and retain occupiers.

severn-trent.description: Severn Trent provides water and wastewater services, with regulated operations serving communities in the Midlands and parts of Wales. Its work includes sourcing and treating drinking water, maintaining pipes and managing sewage collection and treatment. Customer charges and investment returns operate within a regulatory framework that sets service expectations and financial allowances. Revenue is therefore linked to essential network services rather than discretionary purchases. The company must invest continually in infrastructure, environmental performance and resilience. Operating efficiency, leakage, pollution outcomes and customer service affect delivery, while the cost of financing long-term investment is important to the economics of its asset-intensive business.

smith-and-nephew.description: Smith & Nephew develops medical technology used in orthopaedics, sports medicine and wound management. Its products include joint implants, surgical tools and technologies that help clinicians treat injuries and manage wounds. Customers include hospitals, surgeons and other healthcare providers, with revenue generated through equipment and consumable-product sales. Clinical results, ease of use and support for medical professionals are important to adoption. The business combines research, regulated manufacturing and specialist sales relationships. Procedure volumes and healthcare budgets influence demand, while product innovation and reliable supply affect competitiveness. Its portfolio includes both surgical products linked to treatment activity and recurring wound-care requirements.

smiths.description: Smiths Group supplies specialised industrial technology, with engineered products used in demanding applications where reliability and technical performance are important. Its activities include sealing systems associated with John Crane and fluid or gas-handling components associated with Flex-Tek, alongside a portfolio that has been undergoing restructuring. Customers operate in areas such as energy, industry and aerospace, buying equipment and replacement products that support their own systems. Revenue combines original equipment sales with ongoing maintenance-related demand. The business depends on engineering expertise, qualification with customers and dependable supply. Investment cycles, aftermarket activity and changes to the group's portfolio influence the mix and resilience of earnings.

spirax.description: Spirax Group provides technologies for industrial heating and fluid handling. Its businesses include steam-system products, electric heating solutions and Watson-Marlow pumps and fluid-path technologies. Customers use these systems in processes such as sterilisation, food production, chemical processing and pharmaceutical manufacturing. Revenue comes from equipment, components and related support, with replacement and maintenance needs complementing new investment. The company's value lies in controlling temperature and moving fluids reliably in applications where performance can be critical. Technical advice and customer relationships support product selection. Industrial activity, energy-efficiency requirements and demand in healthcare-related manufacturing influence sales across its specialised markets.

sse.description: SSE owns and develops electricity infrastructure, combining regulated networks with renewable and flexible power generation. Its activities include transmission and distribution assets, wind farms, hydroelectric facilities and other generation or storage capacity. Revenue comes through network arrangements and the production or supply of electricity, with different businesses exposed to different pricing mechanisms. Building new infrastructure requires substantial capital and long project schedules. The company is connected to the expansion of electricity demand and the changing generation mix, but financial outcomes depend on execution, financing and regulatory conditions. Weather, power prices and the availability of generating assets also affect performance.

st-jamess-place.description: St. James's Place provides wealth-management services through a network of financial advisers. Clients receive advice on areas such as investments, pensions and financial planning, with assets allocated to the group's range of investment solutions. Revenue is linked to advice and the ongoing administration and management of client money under its charging arrangements. Long-term adviser relationships are central to attracting and retaining customers. The business depends on client confidence, service quality and investment outcomes, while market movements affect the value of assets on which charges may be based. Regulation, the transparency of fees and the delivery of continuing advice are important operating considerations.

standard-chartered.description: Standard Chartered provides banking services with a strong focus on Asia, Africa and the Middle East. It serves companies and institutions through trade finance, payments, lending and capital-markets services, alongside wealth and retail banking. Its international network is useful to clients moving goods, capital and investment across borders. Revenue comes from interest and financial-service fees, with performance influenced by borrowing demand, transaction volumes and market conditions. Customer deposits and other funding support its lending activities. Operating across diverse economies brings opportunities and complexity, making credit assessment, currency management, compliance and local market knowledge central to the business.

tesco.description: Tesco sells groceries and other everyday products through supermarkets, convenience stores and online channels, with the UK its largest market. Its operations also include Booker wholesaling, which supplies retailers and catering businesses, alongside activities such as mobile services. Revenue is driven mainly by product sales, supported by distribution infrastructure and customer relationships through Clubcard. Frequent food purchases create repeat traffic, while different store formats serve a range of shopping needs. The business relies on scale, availability and competitive value. Supplier negotiations, labour and logistics costs, waste control and household spending patterns all influence the profitability of its high-volume retail model.

united-utilities.description: United Utilities provides water and wastewater services in northwestern England. It collects, treats and supplies drinking water and manages sewage through an extensive network of pipes, treatment works and supporting infrastructure. Its income is governed by a regulated framework that determines charges, investment allowances and performance expectations. Customers depend on the service every day, requiring continuous maintenance and long-term planning. The company invests in capacity, resilience and environmental improvements, with service quality and pollution performance important to regulatory outcomes. Financing costs, construction delivery and operating efficiency influence returns in a business where assets last for decades and investment commitments are substantial.

vodafone.description: Vodafone provides mobile and fixed connectivity to consumers and businesses, with operations spanning European and African markets. Its services include voice and data plans, broadband, business networking and connected-device solutions, while African activities also include mobile-money services. Revenue comes from customer subscriptions, usage and commercial service arrangements. Networks require investment in spectrum, equipment and upgrades, making customer scale and efficient operations important. Its business depends on reliable coverage, retention and the ability to offer services that meet changing data needs. Competition, regulation and local economic conditions influence pricing, while portfolio changes can alter the group's geographic exposure and operating structure.

weir.description: Weir supplies engineering equipment and services used mainly in mining and minerals processing. Its products include pumps, wear parts and other systems designed to handle abrasive materials, alongside ESCO equipment components and digital tools. Customers buy new equipment and replacement parts as mines operate, creating an aftermarket business alongside capital-project demand. Products are exposed to heavy wear, making reliability, availability and technical support important. Revenue depends on customer production and investment, while process-efficiency improvements can support demand for upgraded technology. The business combines engineering design, manufacturing and field services, with mining activity and the need to reduce operating costs shaping customer priorities.

whitbread.description: Whitbread operates hotels, with Premier Inn at the centre of its business in the UK and an expanding presence in Germany. It serves leisure and business travellers through a value-focused accommodation offering supported by booking systems, recognised branding and food-and-beverage services. Revenue comes primarily from rooms and related guest spending. Unlike hotel groups based mainly on franchise fees, its model involves substantial operational and property commitments. Occupancy, room rates and the cost of staffing and maintaining hotels influence profitability. Location selection and development spending matter to growth, while travel demand, competition and the maturity of newer hotels affect returns over time.

polar-capital-technology-trust.description: Polar Capital Technology Trust is a listed investment trust specialising in technology and technology-related companies around the world. Its investment manager selects holdings within that broad theme, giving shareholders exposure to areas such as computing, software and digital infrastructure through a single vehicle. Returns reflect changes in portfolio values and income after fees and other costs. The trust's share price may trade at a discount or premium to its net asset value. Its sector focus distinguishes it from diversified global funds, with results influenced by technological change, competitive shifts and how much investors are willing to pay for the companies it holds.

computacenter.description: Computacenter helps large organisations select, obtain, install and operate technology. Its customers include businesses and public-sector bodies that need devices, data-centre infrastructure, networks and related services. Revenue comes from technology sourcing, professional projects and ongoing managed services, combining product transactions with longer-term support relationships. It works with major technology vendors while helping customers integrate equipment and software into their own environments. The business depends on procurement capability, technical staff and reliable service delivery. Customer investment budgets affect product and project activity, while managed services create recurring work. Large contracts and the mix of hardware and services can influence margins and cash flow.

investec.description: Investec provides specialist banking and wealth-related services, with a strong presence in South Africa and the UK. Its clients include businesses, entrepreneurs, professionals and other private customers needing lending, savings, transactional services and financial expertise. Revenue comes from interest and fees, with the mix varying across its banking and investment-related activities. Rather than relying only on a mass-market branch model, it emphasises specialist capabilities and client relationships. Credit quality, funding costs and customer activity influence earnings. The group's cross-market structure also brings currency and regulatory considerations, while capital management and disciplined lending are important to sustaining its financial services operations.

burberry.description: Burberry designs and sells luxury clothing, accessories and related products under its British heritage brand. Its offering includes outerwear, leather goods and fashion collections distributed through directly operated stores, online channels and wholesale partners, with licensing in selected categories. Revenue depends on customer demand, pricing and the mix of products sold. Brand identity, design and retail presentation are central to its positioning, while controlling distribution helps shape the customer experience. Luxury spending can vary with tourism, consumer confidence and regional economic conditions. Inventory management and the cost of stores and marketing influence profitability, making both creative direction and retail execution important.

ig-group.description: IG Group provides online trading and investment services to customers in several international markets. Its offerings include derivatives trading, share dealing and other investment products, with platforms serving different customer needs and regulatory environments. Revenue comes from trading-related charges, spreads and other income associated with client activity and balances. Technology reliability, execution and access to markets are central to the customer proposition. The business is influenced by market volatility and client engagement, but also requires careful management of exposures and operational systems. Regulation governs product availability and customer protections, while acquiring and retaining active clients is important to commercial performance.

tritax-big-box.description: Tritax Big Box REIT owns and develops large logistics properties in the UK, providing space used by retailers, manufacturers and distribution businesses. Its operating assets generate rent, while its land and development activities create opportunities for additional buildings and future income. The business focuses on properties suited to modern supply chains and generally seeks durable tenant relationships. Returns depend on occupancy, lease terms, rental growth and changes in property values. Development requires capital and successful delivery before rent begins. Access to transport and power infrastructure can affect site appeal, while interest rates and financing costs influence the economics of its property investments.

aberdeen-group.description: Aberdeen Group provides investment and wealth-related services, including asset management and platforms used by individual investors and advisers. Its businesses connect customers with funds, portfolios and tools for holding and managing savings. Revenue comes from investment-management fees and platform charges, with the structure varying between services. Market movements influence the value of client assets, while customer inflows and withdrawals affect commercial scale. The group must balance investment expertise with technology and distribution in a competitive savings market. Performance depends on attracting and retaining clients, maintaining efficient operations and offering products that meet changing preferences for advice, self-directed investing and different asset classes.

coca-cola-europacific-partners.description: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners produces and distributes beverages across territories in Europe, Australia and the wider Asia-Pacific region, including the Philippines. It is a bottling partner that manages manufacturing, packaging, logistics and local sales for Coca-Cola and other drinks. Customers include retailers, restaurants and other outlets serving consumers. Revenue comes from beverage sales, with product mix, pack sizes and pricing influencing margins. Its business depends on local distribution reach and efficient production rather than owning the global Coca-Cola brand. Consumer demand, weather and tourism affect volumes, while packaging, transport and ingredient costs shape the economics of supplying large numbers of outlets.

metlen-energy-metals.description: Metlen Energy & Metals combines energy activities with metals production and industrial projects. Its operations include developing and operating power assets, supplying and trading energy, and producing materials such as alumina and aluminium. It also delivers engineering and construction work associated with energy infrastructure. Revenue therefore comes from several industrial value chains, with project income alongside sales of electricity, gas and metals. The combination links technical project capabilities with physical production assets. Performance depends on commodity prices, energy costs and project execution, while investment decisions shape future capacity. The business requires substantial industrial expertise and careful management of capital, contracts and operating requirements.

lion-finance-group.description: Lion Finance Group provides banking and financial services with a focus on Georgia and Armenia. Its businesses serve individuals, small companies and larger corporate customers through lending, deposits, payments and other banking products. Revenue comes from interest and service fees, supported by local customer franchises and digital channels. Economic growth and financial activity in its core markets influence borrowing and transaction demand. As a banking group, it must manage credit losses, funding and regulatory capital while maintaining reliable services. Its geographic concentration makes local economic, currency and political conditions particularly relevant, alongside the execution of its retail and business-banking strategies.

babcock-international.description: Babcock International provides engineering, support and specialist systems for defence and other critical operations. Its activities span marine, nuclear, land and aviation, including maintaining equipment, supporting naval infrastructure and integrating complex systems. Customers include governments and organisations that need assets to remain available and safe over long operating lives. Revenue comes through contracts covering projects and ongoing services, often requiring specialised staff and facilities. Its model depends on technical capability, security requirements and close understanding of customer operations. Contract execution, labour availability and programme timing influence profitability, while defence priorities and infrastructure commitments shape the pipeline of future work.
